question: Explain the HOT FEPR loop as best you can
reframe: the process rule 334 names HOT FEPR — how a player works through outstanding Tasks and then through the Chain, and which condition sends play from each step to the next.
in_one_line: Anything that incurs a Task runs the same loop: clear every Task first, then work the Chain one item at a time through Finalize, Execute, Pass and Resolve — where most steps can send you backwards, which is why one Chain runs the loop many times before play moves on.

steps.heading: H — Handle Outstanding Tasks
steps.body: A Task is anything one or more players must finish before anything else may happen, so nothing else proceeds while one is outstanding. Chain Items created while you work through Tasks are not lost — they sit on the Chain until the Tasks are done. H is also not only the first step: a Task incurred partway through FEPR pauses the process, and you complete the step you are in, handle the Task, then carry on from where you were. That is a pause and resume rather than a restart, which is why no arrow on the map returns here.

cites.quote: A Task is one or more steps or processes that one or more Players must perform before continuing with any other actions.
Whenever a Player takes one or more actions that incur Tasks they should refer to the process of HOT FEPR: Handle Outstanding Tasks; then Finalize, Execute, Pass, Resolve.
In the course of Handling Outstanding Tasks, Chain Items may be added to the Chain. They will remain there until the Tasks are complete.
During the FEPR process, new Tasks may be incurred. Complete the current step of the process and then pause and complete the necessary Tasks before continuing.

exits.when: every outstanding Task is complete and one or more Chain Items are pending

cites.quote: When there are no outstanding Tasks and there are pending Chain Items on the Chain, players should refer to the FEPR process to proceed.

exits.when: every outstanding Task is complete and nothing is pending on the Chain — there is no Chain to work, so the loop does not run

cites.quote: If there are no Outstanding Tasks, no pending Chain Items, no ongoing Showdown or Combat, and it is the Main Phase, the Turn Player receives priority.

steps.heading: F — Finalize
steps.body: The oldest pending item goes first: its controller completes the steps of playing it until it is Finalized or leaves the Chain, and items finalize in the order they were appended. Finalizing is bookkeeping, not a window to act in — it does not pass Priority. Note the numbering: the rules call Finalize "Step 1", so "return to step 1" inside these rules means Finalize, not Handle Outstanding Tasks.

cites.quote: Step 1: Finalize
If there is at least one Chain Item Pending, the controller of the oldest Pending Chain Item must complete the steps of Playing that Pending Item until it is a Finalized Item or leaves the Chain.
Finalizing an item to the chain does not pass Priority.
Chain Items are Finalized in the order they were appended to the Chain.

exits.when: the item just finalized is a Unit, Gear, or an ability that Adds resources — it never waits on the Chain to be answered

cites.quote: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, that item is a Unit, Gear, or an ability that Adds resources, it resolves immediately—Move to Step 4: Resolve.

exits.when: there are still Pending Chain Items after finalizing that one

cites.quote: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, there are still Pending Chain Items, return to step 1. Finalize.

exits.when: nothing is left on the Chain to finalize

cites.quote: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, there are no more items on the chain to be Finalized, the controller of the next item on the chain gains Priority. Move to step 2: Execute.

steps.heading: E — Execute
steps.body: The player with Priority chooses: play something legally timed, or pass. Those are the only two options on offer — the rules give the player with Priority this list and nothing else. "Legally timed" is the constraint that matters: by default cards and activated abilities cannot be played in a Closed State, so what qualifies here is generally something with Reaction.

cites.quote: The player with Priority may do any the following:
Play a Card or Activated Ability that is legally timed.
Cards and Activated Abilities, by default, cannot be played during a Closed State.
A Legally Timed Card or Activated Ability would be one with Reaction or one that will have Reaction when played under appropriate circumstances.
Pass Priority

exits.when: the player with Priority plays a card or activates an ability, which puts new Pending Items on the Chain

cites.quote: Playing a Card or Activated Ability will create one or more Pending Items. Return to Step 1: Finalize.

exits.when: the player with Priority passes instead

cites.quote: The player with Priority passes Priority to the next Player in Turn Order. Proceed to Step 3: Pass.

steps.heading: P — Pass
steps.body: Pass asks one question: has every player passed in sequence without adding anything to the Chain? That is the test for whether the window has actually closed, and playing anything at all resets it.

cites.quote: If all players have passed Priority in sequence without adding any items to the Chain, proceed to Step 4: Resolve.
Otherwise, the player with Priority passes Priority to the next Player in Turn Order. Return to Step 2: Execute.

exits.when: every player has passed in sequence with nothing added to the Chain

cites.quote: If all players have passed Priority in sequence without adding any items to the Chain, proceed to Step 4: Resolve.

exits.when: the sequence of passes is not complete, so Priority moves on to the next player

cites.quote: Otherwise, the player with Priority passes Priority to the next Player in Turn Order. Return to Step 2: Execute.

steps.heading: R — Resolve
steps.body: Exactly one item resolves — the newest Finalized one — and its effects are executed in their entirety. One item, not the whole Chain: what happens next depends entirely on what is still sitting on it, and the three transitions below are the whole answer.

cites.quote: The newest Finalized Chain Item resolves. Execute its game effects in their entirety.
If the Chain is empty, play proceeds in an Open State.

exits.when: the Chain is not empty and one or more items on it are still pending

cites.quote: If the Chain is not empty and there are one or more Pending Items, return to Step 1: Finalize.

exits.when: the Chain is not empty but nothing on it is pending

cites.quote: If the Chain is not empty and there are no Pending Items, the controller of the newest item on the chain gains Priority. Return to Step 2: Execute.

misconceptions.belief: You can respond to a unit being played, the way you respond to a spell.
misconceptions.why_wrong: A Unit resolves the moment it is finalized. It moves straight to Resolve without passing through Execute, so the window in which anyone could answer it never opens.

cites.quote: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, that item is a Unit, Gear, or an ability that Adds resources, it resolves immediately—Move to Step 4: Resolve.

misconceptions.belief: Once you are in FEPR you run it to the end before anything else happens.
misconceptions.why_wrong: A Task incurred during the process interrupts it. You finish the step you are in, handle the Task, and only then continue — which is the H in HOT FEPR doing work in the middle of the loop, not just at its start.

cites.quote: During the FEPR process, new Tasks may be incurred. Complete the current step of the process and then pause and complete the necessary Tasks before continuing.

misconceptions.belief: When everyone passes, the Chain resolves.
misconceptions.why_wrong: One item resolves. If anything is left on the Chain afterwards you go back into the loop — to Finalize if something is pending, to Execute if not — so a Chain of three resolves in three separate passes with a window of opportunity between each.

cites.quote: The newest Finalized Chain Item resolves. Execute its game effects in their entirety. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information on resolving spells. See rule 398. Playing or Activating Abilities for more information on resolving abilities.
If the Chain is not empty and there are one or more Pending Items, return to Step 1: Finalize.
If the Chain is not empty and there are no Pending Items, the controller of the newest item on the chain gains Priority. Return to Step 2: Execute.

considered_rejected.why: Describes when a phase ends once the Chain is empty — the frame around this loop, not a step inside it.
Showdowns are a window FEPR runs inside; the alternation of Focus is a separate process from the Priority passing in step 3.
